text:
Surveillance changes our behavior
Hundreds of thousands of people in Hong Kong are protesting an unpopular new bill which would allow extradition to China. Typically, Hong Kong locals use their rechargeable smart cards to ride the subway. However, during the protests, long lines of people waited to use cash to buy paper tickets (usually something that only tourists do) concerned that they would be tracked for having attended the protests. Would fewer people protest if this was not an option?

In the United States, in 2015 the Baltimore Police Department used facial recognition technology to surveil people protesting the death of Freddie Grey, a young Black man who was killed in police custody, and arrested protesters with outstanding warrants. Mass surveillance could have a chilling impact on our rights to move about freely, to express ourselves, and to protest. “We act differently when we know we are ‘on the record.’ Mass privacy is the freedom to act without being watched and thus in a sense, to be who we really are,” Columbia professor Tim Wu wrote in the New York Times.

Flyer from the company Geofeedia Source
Surveillance disproportionately impacts those who are already marginalized
Surveillance is applied unevenly, causing the greatest harm to people who are already marginalized, including immigrants, people of color, and people living in poverty. These groups are more heavily policed and surveilled. The Perpetual Line-Up from the Georgetown Law Center on Privacy and Technology studied the unregulated use of facial recognition by police, with half of all Americans appearing in law enforcement databases, and the risks of errors, racial bias, misuses, and threats to civil liberties. The researchers pointed out that African Americans are more likely to appear in these databases (many of which are drawn from mug shots) since they are disproportionately likely to be stopped, interrogated, or arrested. For another example, consider the contrast between how easily people over 65 can apply for Medicare benefits by filling out an online form, with the invasive personal questions asked of a low-income mother on Medicaid about her lovers, hygiene, parental shortcomings, and personal habits.

In an article titled Trading privacy for survival is another tax on the poor, Ciara Byrne wrote, “Current public benefits programs ask applicants extremely detailed and personal questions and sometimes mandate home visits, drug tests, fingerprinting, and collection of biometric information… Employers of low-income workers listen to phone calls, conduct drug tests, monitor closed-circuit television, and require psychometric tests as conditions of employment. Prisoners in some states have to consent to be voiceprinted in order to make phone calls.”

Data privacy is a public good, like air quality or safe drinking water
Data is more revealing in aggregate. It can be nearly impossible to know what your individual data could reveal when combined with the data of others or with data from other sources, or when machine learning inference is performed on it. For instance, as Zeynep Tufekci wrote in the New York Times, individual Strava users could not have predicted how in aggregate their data could be used to identify the locations of US military bases. “Data privacy is not like a consumer good, where you click ‘I accept’ and all is well. Data privacy is more like air quality or safe drinking water, a public good that cannot be effectively regulated by trusting in the wisdom of millions of individual choices. A more collective response is needed.”

Unfortunately, this also means that you can’t fully safeguard your privacy on your own. You may choose not to purchase Amazon’s ring doorbell, yet you can still show up in the video footage collected by others. You might strengthen your online privacy practices, yet conclusions will still be inferred about you based on the behavior of others. As Professor Tufekci wrote, we need a collective response.

We don’t have to accept invasive surveillance
Many people are uncomfortable with surveillance, but feel like they have no say in the matter. While the threats surveillance poses are large, it is not too late to act. We are seeing success: in response to community organizing and an audit, Los Angeles Police Department scrapped a controversial program to predict who is most likely to commit violent crimes. Citizens, researchers, and activists in Detroit have been effective at drawing attention to the Detroit Police Department’s unregulated use of facial recognition and a bill calling for a 5-year moratorium has been introduced to the state legislature. Local governments in San Francisco, Oakland, and Somerville have banned the use of facial recognition by police.

WODEMAN
A Romaunce in Three Actes

The Laste Daye II

The next storme came upone a nyght without sterres. The zee struck from two quarters at once; abouve, the sayle bræst loose and floggede the mast like a furieux flagellante. Beneath, the oores took such weyghte that every banke strained to lyfte them from the watere.

Vettore cried commaunds from the decke. Niko came down to the benches with a stycke, though feare made his strokes fall wide. Matteo had eaten no more than a thumb of byscuite in two dayes. He held the shafte opposite Cane, his face pallid in the swyngynge lanterne. On oon false pulle he roose too soone. The greate oore cæm backe agaynst him.

He dropped. Cane saw it across the passauge. The banke behind him was already leanynge into the next stroke. To loose his holde would drive the shaft among six men's faces; to reach the boy he must cross two chained rowes and the running oore. He shouted instead.

“Matteo!”

The boy stirred beneathe the bench, coughed, and brought blode to his lips. Nico ordered him upright. He could not rise. Nico hit him, once, and the Greke called out that his blowes would not mend a broken rib nor empty a drowned lung.

“Then make him pull!” Nico shouted.

Vettor's voice came through the hatch.
“TO PORT! OORES TO PORT!”

No man on the boate knew if he meant the syde or a harbour. They hauled Matteo clear and chained his ankle beside the oore. Cane kept stroke opposite the vacant place while the Greke and Nello took what weyght the boy no lenger bore. In the derke betwixt eche drumbeate Cane heard him trying to breathe.

The gæley survived. At dawn the sea lay quiet, worn out before the men were. Vettore gave no rest. He said the coaste myght be neare, though he had no lond to shew them. Matteo lay in his iron with his eyes shutte. When Cane called, the boy lifted two fingers from the planks. The answer cost him near all the strength he had.

Dayes passede. Matteo lyvede. His caugh softened and then retourned; bruises yellowed; he could sit, and presently make jests of the broth in whych no fishe hadde ever drowned. He coulde not yet pulle an oore. Nico, needing every able backe at the benches, unlocked the boy at daylighte and set him to fyshing from the sterne under wautch. Matteo caught little. The fyrste fish he brought aboord fede four men by the accounte, twelve by the way the morsels treveilede after darke.

One clear nyght the Greke asked leave to go above.

“Thou wilt dive to shore?” Vettor said.

“Yif I could, messere, I should have done so while thou wert dining.”

Niko laughed. Vettor did not, but he let the manne climbe. He came behind him with a cord in his fist and stood watching as the Greke lifted his face unto the sterres.

The Greke studied the heiught of one bryghte point, the drift af cloud, the smell of the wynde. He asked where the moone had risen on two earlier nyghtes and listened to men who had kept watch. His father had once saylede graine into the Blacke See. He himself had treveyllede the northern harbours as a free seaman afore a failed venture and a creditour made a rower of him.

“Thou canst tell our place?” asked Niko.

“I can tell thee where we are likeliest not to be.”

“An admirable service,” Vettor said.

The Greke pointed northward. “The Krymean shore, perauenture. We are nearer than thy feare would have it, faurther than thy hope. Theodoro lieth in those londes; the Genowayes hold their zea-touns alonge the coost. Yif this wynd abideth, we may seek menne who know a harbour.”

Vettor looked into the emptiness. “How many dayes?”

“That dependeth upon the wynde.”

“And yif it turneth?”

“Then it dependeth more.”

It was a poor promesse. On the Santa Marta it passed from bank to bank as rychesse.
For two dayes the captein remembered how to commaund without strykynge. Niko brought the Greke above again at dusk and, once, let him taste a spoon of hot broth. Matteo caught another fish. Goro named the fish a duke on account of its small body and enormous mouth. The Dalmatian demanded the liver as a tax. The black-haired man laughed; he had learnt enough of their quarrels to laugh before the words were translated.

At rest the Greke, Cane, and Nello disputed whether a manne myghte own a road over water.

“He may own a ship,” said Nello.

“He may build one,” said Cane.

“There is difference?”

“A ship hath been made by hondes. The see hath not.”

“A lord may claim both,” said the Greke.

“An emperour may claime the wynde also,” Nello said. 

“When it chaungeth, he will appoint a newe one.”

Nico, crouched near the ladder with his bowl, found himself speaking. “Without a maister, who bringeth the men unto a haven?”

“The man who knoweth the waye,” said the Greke.

“And yif he is a slave?”

“The haven lieth in the same place.”

Nico considered his bowle. He had lived twenty yeres among the Bellani and never heard a sclave answer a question of gouvernement as though his answer matterede. The Greke did not press him. Nello asked for more broth, and the yonge keeper told him he could debate with an empty spoone.

Matteo sat wrapped in saylclothe, trying to clean a hook with numb fyngers. “I shall fish for my owne supper when we reach ashore.”

“And for mine,” said Cane.

“Thou shalt work.”

“At what?”

“Sleeping without iron. Thou promisedst to teach me.”

The mainlander looked down at the silver mark the cuff had made about his left wrist. “A hard trade.”

“I have learnt harder.”

Later, when the otheres slept, he reckoned the shore in his mynde. The Bellani contract had been torn from its floete, its witnesses scauttered, its keeper dead, and its capteine near mad. There might be a Genoway officer willing to sell them onward, or one willing to hear how they had been brought. Cane trusted neither outcome. Yet lond had streetes, tourns, market crowds, a hundred places wherein a manne could be lost unto his owner. With Matteo well enough to waulk, he woulde finde one. He did not tell the buoye. Hope spoken aloud aboord a galeey had a way of entering another man's ledger.

The nyghte of the laste daye began so gently that no manne thought to name it.

Matteo came aboord from the sterne platforme with three little fysh. Niko hadde not locked his ankle anew; the buoy could scarce walke withoute stopping for breath, and there was nowhere to flee upon the open zee. He held the catch up for Goro's judgement. Goro declaured the largest a kynge, the second a byshoppe, and the third a tax collectour, on accounte of its teeth.

“Then the tax collector is mine,” said Matteo.

“Nay. He hath already taken his portioun.”

Nico cleaned them with the narrow knyfe he wore at his belte. He gave the bones unto the pot and the flesche unto Vettore, who looked at the three small bodies and spoke of their insufficiencie. The buoye received some broth at laste. He carried it down the passauge, stopping once to set a spoonful beneath the Dalmatian's nose.

“For my counsel?” the olde man said.

“For thy silence.”

“Thou shalt die in dette.”

Matteo smiled and went on. At Cane's bank he held out the bowl.

“Eat.”

“It is thine.”

“Thou gavest me wautere upon my fyrste daye.”

“And thou hast been repaying that folly since.”

“Then accept the intereste.”

Cane took a mouthfoulle. Across the benches the Greke began, hardly knowing he did so, to hum the olde measure of the gull and the chayne. Matteo joined him in a whisper. For a few strokes of the hearte it seemed possible that they myght reach a shore with the same voices they had broughte into the storme.

*"The gull hath neither lord ne rent,
No seale upon his wing is pent;
He asketh neither duke ne kinge
What leave he hath to flee and singe."*

Matteo joined them wyth the verse he hadde made. The Dalmatian's rough voice followed; Goro beat tyme with a spoone agaynst his knee. Saul knew onely the laste word of every line and sange it as though that were sufficiente. From above, Nico heard them and did not reach for his stycke.

*"Come lowe, come lowe, thou waundering gull,
The pot is warme, the bowle is full;
Yif all we have be scant for two,
Call in a third; we shall make do.."*

*"By dawne we'll finde a willow quay,
A bakehouse waking with the daye;
We'll hang our oores upon a tree,
And call its shade our.."*

Vettor came down the ladder.

The Greke fell quiet. Matteo heard him too late, with the last note yet upon his lips.

“I forbade that songe.”

“It was I,” Matteo said.

Vettor glanced at the Greke. “Thou makest him bold.”

“He is haungry, messere. Haunger doth straunge thyngs unto hearing.”

The captayn's lash found Matteo across the shoulder. Cane rose halfway from his bench; the left wryste-ryng checked him. Matteo set down the bowl before it could be spilt.

“I have ceased,” he said.

“Then prove it.”

The buoy closed his mouth. Vettor awaited, as though silence must be demonstrated over tyme to become credible. At length he climbed aboove. Niko followed, but tourned once towaurd the bowle upon the planks.

The menne slept by wautches. Far into the nyght the wauter lay so calme that the galey's owne timber could be heard settling against itselfe. Cane gave Matteo a look across the passauge. The buoy, curled beneath a torne sayle, lifted one finger: I am awake. Cane lifted his in return. Then he slept.

A crie fetched him out of sleepe.
It came from behynde his backe, beyond the rowes and the stacked coils of coord near the sterne. He could see the little keeper Niko sprawled beside the ladder. Darke blode spread from his temple over the boaurds; his narrow knyfe lay somewhere beyond his outstretched honde. Of Matteo he could see nothynge.

The boy cried agayn.
“Help me!”

Cane turned. The iron bit his left wryste. In the dimmest of the lamplight he made out Vettore's shoulders rising and falling beyonde the coord. A bodie laye beneath them.
Niko had gone below after the captayne slepte. He had brought the last of the fishe broth to Matteo, who was shivering and could scarcely keepe his spoon steadie. Vettor followed him. He saw the bowl, the unchayned buoy, the keeper leaning close, and gave their little misericordaunce a treasonable name. Nico told him he had brought the food himselfe. Vettor struck him with the butt of his own lash. Matteo caught at Vettor's sleeve, begging him to stop. The capetayn turned.

No man at the oores had seen all of this. They heard enough.

“Vettore,” the Greke called. “The boy is down.”

The blows continued.

“Capitaine,” Nello said. “He hath no weapon.”

“He hath a voice,” said Vettor from behynde the coord.

Matteo called Cane's name. On the fyrst cry the mainlander hauled at his ring so savagely that the bench shifted. He heard the buoy cry the second time. On the third he heaurd onely the capitayn.

“God putteth men in degrees,” Vettor shouted. “A kyng above a lourde; a lourde above a maister; a maister above the beest that eateth his bread. Yif the beest may synge, it soon asketh who built the stable. Yif it may aske, it soon demandeth the keye. My father bought this gæley; I have fed ye through pyrates and tempest. The Emperour may stamp a lawe, the duke may stamp a seale, and I have paid good silvere for the right to make either of them move!”

His fist fell agayn. The sound was lowe and heavy. Goro cried to him to stop. The former shield-bearer shouted that he would bear witness. Vettor laughed.

“Unto whom? I shall set thee ashore with thy iron and ask whose worde the harbour will purchase.”

Cane pulled until his honde had no feeling. He put a foot against the bench and wrenched his left wryst in the iron. Somethynge yielded with a sickening little sound. The hond came partway through the ring. The broken joint caught.

He drew breath through his teeth and tried agayn.
“It will not passe,” said the field-labourer behinde him.

“I know.”“Thou wilt tear thy whole arme.”

“I know.”

They heard Matteo call once more, very faintly. Cane strained so hard the edge of the cuff opened his skyn. Beyond the coords came another blow. Then the buoy's voice stopped.

The Greke looked down the passage. Nico lay in reach of Nello's bare feete. Beside the young keeper gleamed the dropped blade.

“Nello.”

“I see it.”

“Thou canst not reach.”

“I see that also.”

The Greke raised both armes. Along the benches heads lifted. The men who had conspired in finger-taps and blynks now understood one another without any signe at all.

“Heave,” he said.

They threw their weyght unto one side. The Santa Marta lurched. The blade shifted no farther than a fingernaile.

Vettor shouted from the stern, but his voice had become a noise among noises.

“Agayn,” said the Greke.

Six oores pressed against the blacke water. Chaynes rang from bank to bank. The galey rolled; Nello's foot caught the knife and lost it.

“A third,” said the Greke.

The Dalmatian braced his oon sound eye upon the passauge. Goro set his back against his banke. Saul, the field-labourer, the ruined shield-bearer, every debtour and outcast who could still command a breath gave it together. Their oores struck the see. The hull heeled; Nello hooked the knife with his toes and sent it clattering beneath the fourth bank.

Cane caught it with his right hand.

For a little while he could do nothyng. His left hond hung in the iron; beyond it the broken wrist had swollen against the cuff. The Greke called his name, the name the maisters used. Cane looked down at the blade and understood the price of crossing the few paces that lay behynde him.

There came from the stern a dull blow, then another. Matteo made no sound.

Cane set the edge against his ruined wryst.

The fyrste cut brought a cry out of him so great that it silenced Vettore. He tried agayne. The knife bit and stopped; blood made the hilt slide in his living hand. He drew the edge to and fro through the ragged flesh. Pale sinewes still held where the skyn hadde paurted, and beneath them the bone grated against the blade. The hand imprisoned in the cuff shook with every stroke. He worked through what would not yield, a little more with each pulle, drawing steel and breath in short, desperate measures. He shrieked once more, a sound he would afterward hear in dreams, though he could never remember making it. From the stern came the thudde of Vettor's fist. Matteo made no answer.

Nello turned his face away. The Greke did not. He kept calling the strookes of the oore lest the boate lie still for the pyrates, or the wynde, or whatever cruel chaunce might yet be following them.

At last the weight of the iron left Cane's arme. His severed hand remained within the ring. He stumbled in his ankle-chaine and near fell; the field-labourer caught him by the coat and thrust him toward the stern.

“Goe.”

Cane went.

He founde Vettor bent over the buoy. The capetayne had exhausted werds and continued with his honds. Cane struck him from behynde. They felle together against a water cask, which burst its hoops and poured its little treasure between them. Vettor clawed for a hold; Cane drove him aside. Nello, still chained, caught the captayn's leg as he tried to rise. Goro shouted for a coord. Above all their voices Cane heard Matteo breathing.

He went to him.

The buoy's face had altered beyond any bruise he had ever carried. One cheek had been beaten hollow; through its torn flesh Cane saw white splinters of the crushed bone. Blood darkened the cavity beneath his eye and welled at the corner of his mouth. His little fyshynge honds lay open upone the boords. Cane knelt in the spreading blood and gathered Matteo's shoulders, then stopped, afraid that even his tenderness might hurt him.

“Matteo.”

The eye that could still open found him.

“Thou camest.”

“Aye.”

“I thought,” said the boy. Breath failed him. “I thought thou couldst not.”

“So did I.”

Cane touched the unbroken side of his face. Tears came, furious and helpless. He had never found a use for them aboord the galeey, yet now they fell over Matteo's hair and onto the deck where a whole company wautched.

“The shore,” the boy whispered.

“We were seeking it.”

“Are we nigh?”

The Greke, kneeling by Nico, raised his head. He could have offered a bearing, a measure of cloud, the likelihood of lond beyond the derke. He said nothynge.

“Nigher than yesterday,” Cane answered.

Matteo breathed a little laugh. “That is what thou sayest whan thou knowest not.”

“Thou hast learnt too much from me.”

“Enough to miss thee.”

Cane bent lowe. He saw the buoy's breath lessen and could neither lend him his owne nor bargayne for another. From the benches came the small noises of menne setting down their oores. Someone covered Nico, who yet lived, against the cold. The Greke stood beside the captayne; no one asked Vettor for an order.

“Lucia,” Matteo said.“I remember her.”

“Tell them.”

“Whom?”

“Any man that asketh.” The boy swallowed with pain. “Tell him she was my mother. Tell him I stole the bread for her.”

“I shall.”

“And tell him,” Matteo whispered, “that I would have fyshed for us both.”

Cane bowed his head against the boy's hair. Beneath him the galey moved on, though no drum commanded it. Matteo drew another labouring breath.

“Thou knowest my name,” he said. “All this tyme, I have not knowen thine. What name shall I keepe for thee?”

Cane laid his living hand about Matteo's face.
“Brando.”

Matteo's lips shaped the name. No voice came with it.

His breaust rose once beneath Brando's arme. It sank, and would not rise agayn.

Brando waited.

He watched for the next breath as menne wautch the farre zee for a sayle they have lost in the derke. The buoy gave him none.

Behind him, Vettor Bellani tore his leg free of Nello's grasp. He caught the ladder and hauled himselfe upright, blode running from his nose.

“Iron,” Vettore said. “Put him backe in iron.”

Brando lowered Matteo to the boards. At his knee lay Nico's small knife, the edge dulled upon his owne wrist-bone. He took it up.

Vettor met him against an oore-bench. The blade bit into the captayn's coate and snagged against a buckle. Vettore caught Brando's maimed left arme and wrung it. The crye that came from Brando might have belonged to another man. They went down together. The captayne struck Brando's right wryst against the gunwale; the knyfe skittered through an open oore-port and was gonne unto the blacke see.

Vettore got his knee beneath him. He struck Brando in the mouth and made for the ladder. Brando dragged him backe by the hair. They felle against the bench. The capetain rose halfway; Brando brought him down agayne.

He beat him with his right fyste.

The firste blow split his knuckles. The next took skyn from the capitayn's browe. Vettor struck backe, clawed, drove an elbow into Brando's throat. Brando tasted his owne blode and could no lenger tell it from the blode upon his face. He struck until his fingers swelled too greatly to close.

“Brando,” called Nello. “He is down.”

“Enough,” said Goro.

He heard neither.

With his swollen right hond he held Vettor to the boards. Then he raised the ruin of his left. White bone stood forth from the torn flesh where the knife hadde failed to leave a clean end. He brought it down upon the captayn's face. Agayn. Upon his brest. Agayn. Bone rasped against tooth and oak, splintering to a jagged edge. What had been Brando's arme became a blade by the measure of the blowes he could not cease to give.

The men called unto him, each in his owne tongue. The Dalmatian cursed him. Nello begged. Saul cried, “Brando!” Still Brando saw onely red: red upon the plankes, red upon the captayn's open coate, red where Matteo lay beyond them. The sound of striking filled the galley after Vettor had made his last sound.

The Greke knelt beside Nico and found the Bellani skeleton-key at the young keeper's belt. One turn loosed the iron from his ankles. He crossed the passauge and caught Brando from behynde, both armes about his breaust.

Brando fought the embrace as though it were another chayne.

“No more,” the Greke said into his ear. “There is no more of him.”

At their feete Vettor lay loose as a pig-carcasse fallen from the butcher's hooke. Brando was red with blode from browe to heel. Beneath it his eyes were open, though they looked at nothynge the Greke could see.

“Matteo,” the Greke said.

The name reached him.

His bodie gave way at laste. The Greke held him whilst another man bounde the bleedyng arme in torne saylcloth. Across the benches the little keye passed from hond to hond. The iron opened; none commanded it. Beside them Matteo lay under the Dalmatian's cloak, his fyshing handes at rest.

At dawne the oores entered the water together. No drum gave the measure. They bore Matteo toward the shore he hadde asked to see; the galey went where her men willed.

Law enforcement officers lose qualified immunity when a plaintiff proves both that the officer violated a “Constitutional Right” and that “The Right” was clearly established at the time of the incident.

How Qualified Immunity Fails in Court
Under the two-part test used by courts, an officer is denied protection if: 

•A constitutional violation occurred: 
The officer's conduct (such as using excessive force or conducting an unlawful search) violated the U.S. Constitution. 

•The law was clearly established: 
Existing precedent (from the U.S. Supreme Court, a federal appeals court, or a state supreme court) made it apparent and obvious to a reasonable officer that their specific conduct was unlawful. 

Scenarios Where Immunity Does Not Apply
Qualified immunity protects civil servants from personal monetary liability in civil lawsuits, but it does not apply in other contexts: 
•Criminal charges: 
Qualified immunity only shields officers from civil suits, meaning it offers no protection against criminal prosecution by state or federal authorities. 

•Municipal liability: 
The defense applies to individual officers, not to local government entities or cities themselves. 

•Injunctive relief: 
Plaintiffs seeking court orders to stop a specific police policy or practice rather than financial damages can bypass the doctrine

FYI : For anyone who doesn’t know what is meant by a “1983”
Section 1983 (codified at 42 U.S. Code § 1983) is a federal civil rights law that allows people to sue state and local government officials who violate their constitutional rights or federal laws while acting under government authority. 

Originally enacted as part of the Civil Rights Act of 1871 (also known as the Ku Klux Klan Act), the statute was designed during Reconstruction to protect newly freed individuals and combat lawlessness by public officials. 
Today, it serves as a primary legal tool to hold government actors accountable. 

How Section 1983 Works
•Does not create rights: 
Section 1983 does not grant new civil rights; instead, it provides a legal mechanism to enforce rights that already exist under the U.S. Constitution or federal statutes. 

•Under color of law: 
The defendant must have acted "under color of state law," meaning they used their official position, badge, or government authority to commit the wrongful act. 

•Proving a claim: 
A plaintiff must show that a state or local actor deprived them of a federal right and that this violation caused actual harm or injury. 

Common Examples of Claims
•Police misconduct: 
Cases involving excessive force, police brutality, wrongful arrest, or false imprisonment. 

•Jail and prison conditions: 
Situations where correctional staff show "deliberate indifference" to an inmate's serious medical needs or safety. 

•Constitutional violations: 
Infringements on free speech, religious freedom, or due process protections guaranteed by the First, Fourth, and Fourteenth Amendments. 

Available Remedies
•Damages: 
Financial compensation for medical bills, lost wages, pain and suffering, or wrongful death.

•Injunctive relief: 
Court orders requiring a government agency or official to change a policy or stop specific misconduct.

•Attorney's fees: 
Compensation to help cover the legal costs of bringing the lawsuit

Remove all heart problems, strokes, leukemia, cancer, disease, infirmary, injury, sickness, fatigue, or pain, and renew his strength, energy, and vitality. Your healing power knows no equal, and in our times of need, we implore you to mend not only our physical wounds but the scars that mar our souls. Pour forth your divine grace upon us, dear Mother, and restore us to a state of wholeness, that we may bear witness to the miracle of your love. Amen.

Prayer to St. Jude:

Oh glorious apostle St. Jude, faithful servant and friend of Jesus, the name of the traitor who delivered thy beloved Master into the hands of His enemies has caused thee to be forgotten by many, but the Church honors and invokes thee universally as the patron of hopeless cases--of things despaired of. Pray for me who am so miserable; make use, I implore thee, of that particular privilege accorded thee of bringing visible and speedy help where help is almost despaired of. Come to my assistance in this great need, that I may receive the consolations and succor of heaven in all my necessities, tribulations and sufferings, particularly—completely heal from all heart problems, injuries, cancer and diseases, and protect  Kramer —and that I may bless God with thee and all the elect throughout eternity. Prayer to St. Michael (Long Version)

O Glorious Prince of the heavenly host, Saint Michael the Archangel, defend us in the battle and fearful warfare that we are waging against the principalities and powers, against the rulers of this world of darkness, against the evil spirits. Come thou to the assistance of men, whom Almighty God created immortal, making them in His own image and likeness and redeeming them at a great price from the tyranny of Satan. Fight this day the battle of the Lord with thy legions of holy Angels, even as of old thou didst fight against Lucifer, the leader of the proud spirits and all his rebel angels, who were powerless to stand against thee, neither was their place found any more in heaven. And that great dragon was cast forth, the ancient serpent, who is called the devil and satan, who seduces the whole world; and he was cast forth upon Earth, and his angels were sent with him.

But behold! the ancient enemy of mankind and a murderer from the beginning has been fiercely aroused. Changing himself into an angel of light, he goes about with the whole multitude of the wicked spirits to invade the earth and blot out the Name of God and of His Christ, to plunder, to slay, and to consign to eternal damnation the souls that have been destined for a crown of everlasting life. This wicked serpent, like an unclean torrent, pours into men of depraved minds and corrupt hearts the poison of his malice, the spirit of lying, impiety and blasphemy, and the deadly breath of impurity and every form of vice and iniquity.

Be favorable to Thy Church, the Bride of the Lamb without spot, whose enemies have filled to overflowing with gall and inebriated with wormwood. They have laid profane hands upon Her most sacred treasures. Where the See of the most blessed Peter and the Chair of Truth has been constituted as a light to the nations, there they have placed a throne of their abomination and impiety; so that with the Pastor struck, they may prevail to disperse the flock.

Therefore, most invincible Leader, be with the people of God against this spiritual wickedness and bring about victory. Thou art venerated by Holy Church as Her guard and patron; Thou art glorified as our defender against the impious powers of earth and of hell. Unto thee the Lord hath handed over the souls of the redeemed to be placed in happiness above.

Entreat the God of peace, to obliterate satan beneath our feet, lest he prevail further to hold men captive, and to injure the Church. Offer our prayers in the sight of the Most High, so that the mercy of the Lord may swiftly overtake us, and apprehend the dragon, the ancient serpent, who is the devil and satan, and send him bound into the abyss, so that he may seduce the nations no more.

Henceforth having been confided to thy escort and protection, we sacred ministers by the authority of the Holy Mother Church [if recited by a cleric of the order of exorcist or above, say instead: by our authority], do undertake to repel the infestations of diabolical deceit in the Name of Jesus Christ, Our God and Lord.

Behold the Cross of the Lord; be scattered hostile powers.
The Lion of the tribe of Juda has conquered, the root of  Kramer.
Let Thy mercies be upon us, O Lord.
As we have hoped in Thee.
O Lord, hear my prayer.
And let my cry come unto Thee.
The Lord be with you all.
And with thy spirit.

Let us pray.
O God, and Father of Our Lord Jesus Christ, we invoke Thy Holy Name, and we humbly implore Thy clemency so that, through the intercession of Mary, the Immaculate ever-Virgin Mother of God, of blessed Michael the Archangel, of blessed Joseph, the Spouse of the same blessed Virgin, of the blessed Apostles Peter and Paul, and of all the Saints, Thou may deign to offer us aid against satan, and all the other unclean spirits, who wander through the world to injure the human race and to destroy souls. We ask this through Christ Our Lord. Amen.

By the power of the Holy Spirit and by His authority, I ask Jesus Christ to break any and all curses, hexes, vexes, jinks, spells, and all wrong prayers and words, and to send them all back to where they came from, if it be His Holy Will. I beseech Thee, Lord Jesus Christ, to protect us by pouring Thy Precious Blood on us; myself, my family, my friends, and all those I pray and intercede for; which Thou hast shed for us and I ask Thee to command that any departing spirits leave quietly, without disturbance, and go straight to Thy Cross to be disposed of as Thou sees fit. I place myself, my family, my friends, and all those I pray and intercede for, and all things I pray and intercede for under the protection of the Blood of Jesus Christ which He has shed for us. Tripo P2.0 adds native quad topology and smart UV

It’s Monday, September 28, 2026, and we’ve got some exciting news from the world of 3D modeling software. Tripo has just released a major update to their platform, bringing with it several impressive new features that could shake up the industry.

So, what exactly is this all about? Why should you care? And how does it impact your day-to-day work?
What Tripo P2.0 Brings to the Table

Tripo’s latest iteration, P2.0, introduces several key advancements aimed at making 3D modeling faster and more efficient.
Native Quad Topology
One of the standout features is native quad topology. This means that models are generated with a clean 4-sided grid structure, complete with proper edge flow and anatomical loops around joints, eyes, and mouths. The mesh is essentially ready for rigging and skinning straight out of the box.
Game Budget Polygon Count
Tripo now limits the polygon count to around 25,000 quads or roughly 50,000 triangles. This makes it a perfect fit for low-poly or mid-poly assets in Unity or Unreal Engine, without overwhelming your game’s performance.
Spatial Diffusion Architecture
The model generates its base form quickly and then refines the final mesh with textures within just 2 to 3 minutes on average. It's like having a fast sketch that becomes polished art in no time.
Clean Albedo/Delighting
Tripo has improved how baked lighting and shadows are removed from textures, ensuring colors look neutral and accurate when used in engines with dynamic lighting.
Smart UV: The Real Star of the Show

The real eye-catcher is the new Smart UV feature. This AI-driven tool handles UV unwrapping like a pro:
Semantic Seam Placement
It understands the anatomy and geometry of your model, placing seams where they make sense—like on the back or under the chin—to avoid visible cuts in the final product.
Speed
Unwrapping low-poly characters or props takes just 5 seconds. That’s lightning fast!
Support for Custom Meshes
Smart UV isn’t limited to Tripo-generated models; it works with any OBJ/FBX mesh you import. This is a huge win for those who like to mix and match.
Variability and Free Retries
If the initial unwrap doesn’t work out, you can generate alternative layouts until you find one that fits your needs perfectly.
Pricing Breakdown

Here’s how it works:
• Freebies: Two models are free even without a subscription.
• Pro/Max/Team Plans: After those two free models, Smart UV costs 20 credits per model. You get three free retries for each model on these plans.
• Free/Starter Users: Beyond the initial two free models, you can’t continue using Smart UV unless you upgrade to a paid plan.
So What Changes for You?

If you’re into game development or any kind of 3D modeling where speed and efficiency are key, Tripo’s new features could be a real game-changer. The native quad topology and clean polygon counts mean less manual cleanup work, while the Smart UV tool streamlines your workflow significantly.

But there’s also an awkward bit: why should you trust this new AI-driven approach? It’s all well and good to see impressive demos, but how does it hold up in real-world projects?
What's Stored

Tripo P2.0 stores generated models and their associated textures, UV maps, and other metadata necessary for rendering and editing within the platform. However, it doesn’t store any personal data or user-specific information unless explicitly provided by you.
What’s Excluded

The platform does not include advanced sculpting tools, high-resolution texture baking beyond basic albedo maps, or support for extremely complex geometries that require manual intervention. Additionally, Tripo P2.0 does not offer real-time collaboration features or version control systems.
User Controls

Users have full control over their generated models and can export them in various formats such as OBJ, FBX, and STL. You also retain ownership of the intellectual property rights for any models you create using Tripo’s tools.
Availability

Tripo P2.0 is available now to all users with a Pro/Max/Team subscription plan. Free and Starter plans can access limited features but will need to upgrade to use Smart UV fully.
What This Does Not Prove

While the new features look promising, they don’t necessarily prove that Tripo’s approach is superior in every aspect of 3D modeling. There are still limitations and areas where traditional methods might be more effective or necessary for specific tasks.

For instance, while Smart UV handles basic unwrapping with ease, it may struggle with highly detailed models requiring intricate seam placement. Similarly, the native quad topology works well for standard characters but might not cater to complex anatomical structures that require manual adjustments.
Practical Takeaway

For those who need to churn out high-quality models quickly without sacrificing too much on detail, Tripo P2.0 offers a compelling solution. The combination of native quad topology and Smart UV can significantly reduce the time spent on manual cleanup and optimization, making it easier to focus on creative aspects rather than technical minutiae.

Discuss away, and let’s see where this takes us!

Congresswoman,

I zoomed in on the middle photo. I really did. "New Album. Enter a name for this album: Supporting Small Businesses." Cancel. Save.

Your team screenshotted the photo-op folder... while they were still NAMING the photo-op folder.

I laughed out loud. A sitting congresswoman accidentally posted the receipt for her own photo op.

That isn't a collage. That's a confession with a Cancel button. And honestly? Cancel is the right choice. Your voting record already clicked it.

So let's talk about what didn't make the album.

NFIB is the largest small-business group in the country. Every Congress, they score members on the votes that actually hit Main Street. Your score in the 118th: 11 percent. Your score in the 119th: zero.

Zero.

I teach high school. I've handed back tests where a kid wrote his name, drew a dinosaur, and still scored higher than that. The wheel is spinning, but the hamster clocked out a long time ago.

You brought pictures, so I'll use them.

THE ICE CREAM WINDOW

You cosponsored the Raise the Wage Act. $17 an hour by 2030. It also phases out the tip credit, and it wipes out the youth wage. Then, apparently not satisfied, you signed onto the Living Wage For All Act, which heads toward $25.

The CBO looked at a plain $15 floor and estimated about 1.3 million lost jobs in its middle estimate. Not a Republican think tank. The CBO.

Who gets cut first? The 16-year-old scooping cones at that window. The kid in your photo op is the kid your bill fires. Not exactly the sharpest tool in the shed, that plan.

And this is where I stop being amused.

I teach CTE in a high-need, high-risk district. Most of my kids qualify for free lunch. Do you know what they want more than almost anything? A first job. Not a handout. A JOB. A place that will take a chance on a 16-year-old with no experience, pay him what the work is worth, and teach him to show up on time. That first job is the most important rung on the ladder. It builds the résumé that gets the second job, which gets the third.

Your bill saws that rung off. Then you pose next to the ladder.

Now, your party finds racism in math, in maps, in grammar, in the thermostat setting. So let's go looking in the one place where it's actually written down in black and white. The Congressional Record. And the minimum wage.

The Davis-Bacon Act, the federal wage floor on construction. Rep. Clayton Allgood, a Democrat from Alabama, stood on the House floor and complained about a contractor bringing "cheap colored labor" north to compete with white workers. Rep. John Cochran, a Democrat from Missouri, grumbled about Southern contractors showing up with low-paid Black mechanics. Their fix? A wage floor. Price the Black worker out of the job, and the white worker keeps it. That wasn't an unintended consequence. That WAS the intent.

Go back further. Princeton economist Thomas Leonard wrote a whole book, Illiberal Reformers, on the Progressive Era economists who sold the minimum wage precisely because it would push "unemployables" out of work. Black workers. Immigrants. Women. The disabled. They weren't embarrassed. They put it in print.

Overseas? In South Africa, white unions pushed "equal pay" wage floors in the 1920s for a very simple reason. If a mine owner had to pay a Black worker the same rate as a white one, he'd hire the white one. Walter Williams documented the whole thing in South Africa's War Against Capitalism.

And here at home, Williams pointed out that in 1948, Black teenagers actually had a slightly LOWER unemployment rate than white teenagers, and they worked at higher rates. Then the floor kept climbing. And climbing. Today Black teen unemployment regularly runs about double the white teen rate. Milton Friedman called the minimum wage one of the most anti-Black laws on the books. He wasn't being clever. He was reading the numbers.

So let me get this straight. A policy with racist intent in 1931, racist results in 2026, and you want to make it BIGGER. You say you fight systemic racism. Congresswoman, this IS the system. You're just the newest person feeding it. About as bright as a burnt-out lightbulb.

Jim Quinn's first law of liberalism: it always produces the exact opposite of its stated intent. Law #9 finishes the thought: to liberals, intentions matter more than outcomes. Your intention is a "living wage." The outcome is a Black teenager in the Mon Valley who never gets hired in the first place. Zero dollars an hour is not a living wage.

THE FAMILY RESTAURANTS

Small restaurants run on 3 to 8 percent margins. Pull the tip credit and the owner has three choices: raise prices, cut hours, or buy a kiosk. Funny how none of those made the album. And the servers who clear more in tips than your $17? Many of them lose out, because the owner can't afford to staff the floor anymore. Whoever drafted that is a few fries short of a Happy Meal.

THE CREW OUTSIDE SATIRA'S

You reintroduced the PRO Act. The ABC test turns independent contractors (who ARE small businesses, by the way) into somebody else's employees. The joint-employer rule turns a local franchise owner into a footnote in corporate's union negotiations. California tried the ABC test with AB5 and had to carve out a long list of professions when freelancers, musicians, and writers started screaming. You watched that train wreck and said, "Let's take it national." Not exactly working with a full deck.

THE NEON SIGN

Energy. You voted NO on the PERMIT Act. NO on SPEED. NO on the LNG bill. NO on REFINER. Fuel and electricity sit near the top of every small-business survey, every year. Guess who pays the power bill on that pretty neon sign in photo seven? Hint: not the dim bulb standing in front of it.

THE COFFEE CUPS

Let me try a radical idea on you. A wage is a voluntary agreement. The owner offers. The worker accepts. If nobody accepts, the owner raises the offer or closes the doors. That's not exploitation. That's how every job you've ever had worked too.

The owner in your picture put up her savings. Signed a lease. Maybe a second mortgage. She carries ALL the risk. If the business fails, the workers go find other jobs. She loses everything. And your answer is to hand her a bigger bill, then drop by for a latte and a photo. All foam, no latte.

A wage the business can't pay is not a raise. It's a pink slip with a nicer name. No first job, no résumé, no second job. Just a government check and a permanent underclass that keeps voting for whoever promises the next one. Very convenient for your party. Not so great for my students.

Meanwhile, McDonald's and Walmart already pay above minimum wage and promote crew kids into six-figure store manager jobs, no college debt required. That ladder WORKS. You keep sawing the bottom rung off and calling it compassion. A few sandwiches short of a picnic.

So here's my question, Congresswoman, and I'd genuinely love an answer. What have you actually DONE for these businesses? Not posed with. Not photographed. VOTED for. Name one bill that lowered their costs. One.

The elevator doesn't quite reach the top floor on this one, so take the stairs if you need to. I'll wait.

What's next? A photo tour of the same shops right after voting against every bill they begged for... oh wait. I'm told you already did that. Nine pictures' worth. One of them was the folder name.

At this rate, your next bill will be Free Ice Cream Mondays, and the ice cream shop just eats the cost. Then the Fair Grades Act, where kids with a 4.0 donate GPA points to the kids who skipped class all semester. It's only common sense. This isn't radical.

But what do I know, I am only a teacher who actually read the Congressional Record instead of the photo captions.

text:
one important realization that i had not too long ago is that enjoying the process of something is way more valuable than the destination. ofc this is easier said than done.

i've had many instances where i was obsessed with the goal. for example, when i pursued hard stuff like gpu programming, i was more obsessed with getting good at it than enjoying the process of learning and growing. predictably, i had the biggest and baddest burnout after my gpu programming stint. enjoying the process is way healthier and makes you less prone to burnout.

i haven't had a lot of success with this yet, since it's a recent reframe that i'm trying, and i don't have enough improvements in my quality of life to claim that it's working perfectly. but generally, a few things have helped me.

first off, focusing on the subgoals within a larger goal. for example, to get to a larger goal, you have to do x, y, and z. you have to enjoy and appreciate achieving x, y, and z by themselves, and also celebrate yourself for achieving them. i think this reframe has worked wonders for me in terms of morale during my job search, which is important to manage.

second, and more importantly, you should also reframe your failures or mistakes. people generally say that when you fail, you have to look at the lessons from it, but this can be superficial. it takes time, but you have to learn to see the plus points of a failure, even if it stings, and also focus on the positive feelings you had during the process of pursuing something rather than the bitterness and nervousness that came with the anticipation of failure or the failure itself.

one good example would be my recent experience with an interview process that i failed, and honestly, it broadened my horizons. even though i didn't get in, i was able to see the inside of a software company and get a feel for what it's like in flashy big tech companies and startups. it also made me believe in myself more because i passed exams that were constructed to be hard on purpose.

so even though i didn't get the offer, i was still able to learn and move forward. it sucked a lot, and i was genuinely excited about getting an offer, but overall i was able to make the most out of it. ofc my example is much richer than other forms of pursuits, but i hope i got the idea across.

the most important part is the ability to compress. it's impossible not to feel embarrassment, boredom, or fear during a stressful situation or a high-stakes pursuit, but humans are memory-bound creatures, and we're excellent at compressing and reframing ground truths to better support our own narrative and self-identity.

so influencing this process and learning to appreciate a time when you felt incredible embarrassment, fear, or self-doubt, and even romanticizing it a little, is extremely important. ofc at the start i think it will be conscious, but ideally it eventually becomes subconscious, and i think that's a powerful way to live.

these two reframes have allowed me to become more resilient and also feel more at peace. nothing feels impossible anymore, and i also don't pursue anything that i honestly don't think i want to pursue. it's a much more fulfilling way to live, only doing and learning the things i actually want to do inherently.

text:
$HDSN seems like an intriguing risk/reward here over a multi-year horizon. Set up where commodity price-linked earnings are set to inflect meaningfully higher on the back of supply/demand mismatch, partially created by regulatory change. 

~$220mm market cap with a ~$20mm net cash position. It is one of the largest refrigerant reclaimers/resellers in the US, has been rolling up smaller players, and partnering to improve its reclamation tech. Business fundamentals (and stock price) are almost entirely driven by HFC refrigerant pricing. We’ve seen significant price declines over the last 4 years post a regulatory-driven run up from 2020-2022 (AIM Act). EBITDA peaked at ~$140mm in 2022 and LTM EBITDA sits at ~$19mm.

The AIM act has been discussed on here so I won’t go deep into it. The EPA effectively mandates shutdowns of production and consumption of older refrigerant chemistries and requires a transition to more environmentally friendly refrigerants. 

A big update to AIM regs went into effect in July 2026, allowing installation of older HFC-dependent HVAC equipment for to continue for another ~6 years beyond what original phaseout. Why does this matter? There is pretty much no new HFC supply coming on market (some even shutting down), but the equipment requiring this refrigerant is continuing to be installed. This will create increased demand for the reclaimed HFC refrigerants that HDSN sells. Tightening S/D should drive prices higher. 

While refrigerant market pricing is somewhat opaque, we’ve seen refrigerant prices 3x-10x in Europe and Australia on these supply phaseouts. We’ve even seen it in 2020-2022 in the US upon initial AIM implementation.

What really has me intrigued is Hartree continues to buy shares and took ownership >10%. They are a commodities/cyclicals shop, and the continued buying makes me wonder if they see a similar dynamic about to unfold.

The big risks are if we see voluntary transition to newer refrigerants, refrigerant dumping into the US, regulatory changes loosening S/D, and execution.

HDSN has a clean balance sheet, continues to consolidate the market, and the commodity it sells could see a pricing super cycle over the next few years. Earnings power is meaningfully depressed relative to both mid cycle and peak levels. Lastly, I like that this isn’t an AI play and offers high idio in a very niche market. 

Would love to hear any thoughts, especially color on HFC refrigerant pricing and channel activity!

Class is in session, Senator. You're just not going to like the lesson plan. Your thinking cap is on backwards, and I'm pretty sure it's on the wrong head.

Nine percent inflation. Record gas prices. Grocery bills through the roof. Then ask them if they want to go back.

I think you've spent so many years being the loudest guy in the room that you forgot to check whether anybody in the room was actually doing better. They weren't. They aren't. And you're still passing the collection plate.

You've been wrong so long that even a broken clock feels sorry for you. At least the clock is right twice a day.

The oligarchs don't want it all, Bernie. The oligarchs want you to buy their phone, drive their car, and use their internet, and if you don't want to, you don't have to. Nobody's making you. YOU want it all. Their money, my money, your neighbor's money, and my grandkids' money. And if we say no, you'll just pass a law.

That's the difference between a businessman and a politician. One of them has to earn your money. The other one just takes it.

But what do I know? I'm only a physics teacher and a retired Army medic who does the "educate" part of your slogan for a living, which is one more part than you've managed in thirty-five years.

Clifford Lee Burton (February 10, 1962 – September 27, 1986) was an American musician who served as the bassist for the thrash metal band Metallica from 1982 until his death in 1986. He is renowned for his musicianship and influence.

Burton's early musical ventures include performing in bands such as EZ-Street and Agents of Misfortune, and frequently collaborating with guitarist Jim Martin. While performing in Los Angeles with Trauma, he was discovered by James Hetfield and Lars Ulrich who asked him to replace bassist Ron McGovney in Metallica. After the release of the band's first two albums, Kill 'Em All (1983) and Ride the Lightning (1984), Burton and Metallica achieved a worldwide breakthrough with Master of Puppets (1986), often cited as both the band's best work and one of the best metal albums of all time.

While touring in 1986 to support Master of Puppets, Burton was killed when the band's tour bus was involved in an accident. He received a posthumous writing credit on ...And Justice for All (1988) for the song "To Live Is to Die" and was posthumously inducted to the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as a member of Metallica in 2009. He also appeared in a 2011 Rolling Stone readers' poll recognizing the greatest bassists of all time,[1] and in Rolling Stone's list of the 50 greatest bass players of all time.[2]

Death
Burton's final performance with Metallica on September 26, 1986 was hosted at Solnahallen in Stockholm, Sweden on the Damage Inc. tour in support of the Master of Puppets album.[23] Their next scheduled show at the Saga Theater in Copenhagen, Denmark[24] had their tour bus driving south overnight along European route E4 (now G 557). Band members complained that the bunks on their tour bus were unsatisfactory and uncomfortable. The story of how Burton won the bunk differs between the two band members; as Kirk Hammett stated on VH1's Behind the Music, he and Burton drew cards, and Burton picked the ace of spades, thereby getting the first choice of bunk. Burton told Hammett "I want your bunk". Hammett replied "Fine, take my bunk, I'll sleep up front, it's probably better anyway".[25] However, Ulrich's version of the event was that Hammett and Burton drew straws, while Burton drew the long straw, winning the choice of bunk.[26] Burton was sleeping when, according to the driver, shortly before 7 a.m. on September 27, the bus skidded off the road 12 miles [19 km] north of Ljungby, just north of Dörarp,[27] and flipped onto the grass in Kronoberg County.[28] With no safety restraints on the bunks, Burton was thrown violently through one of the windows of the bus, which fell on top of him right afterwards, killing him instantly. He was 24 years old.

The bus driver later claimed that the crash was caused by the bus hitting a patch of black ice on the road, but Hetfield later stated that he first believed the bus flipped because the driver was intoxicated. Hetfield also claimed that he walked a lengthy distance along the road unsuccessfully searching for the point in which the bus lost traction from the black ice. When local freelance photographer Lennart Wennberg (who attended the crash-scene the following morning) was asked in a later interview about the likelihood that black ice caused the accident, he said it was "out of the question" because the road was dry and the temperature around 36 °F (2 °C), too warm for ice. This was confirmed by police who, like Hetfield, also found no ice on the road. Ljungby detective Arne Pettersson was reported in a local newspaper to have said the tracks at the accident site were exactly like ones seen when drivers fall asleep at the wheel. However, the driver stated under oath that he had slept during the day and was fully rested; his testimony was confirmed by the driver of a second tour bus that was carrying the band's crew and equipment.[27] The driver was determined not at fault for the accident and no charges were brought against him.[29]

Burton's body was cremated and the ashes were scattered at the Maxwell Ranch.[30] At the ceremony, the song "Orion" was played. Clifford Lee Burton (February 10, 1962 – September 27, 1986) was an American musician who served as the bassist for the thrash metal band Metallica from 1982 until his death in 1986. He is renowned for his musicianship and influence.

Burton's early musical ventures include performing in bands such as EZ-Street and Agents of Misfortune, and frequently collaborating with guitarist Jim Martin. While performing in Los Angeles with Trauma, he was discovered by James Hetfield and Lars Ulrich who asked him to replace bassist Ron McGovney in Metallica. After the release of the band's first two albums, Kill 'Em All (1983) and Ride the Lightning (1984), Burton and Metallica achieved a worldwide breakthrough with Master of Puppets (1986), often cited as both the band's best work and one of the best metal albums of all time.

While touring in 1986 to support Master of Puppets, Burton was killed when the band's tour bus was involved in an accident. He received a posthumous writing credit on ...And Justice for All (1988) for the song "To Live Is to Die" and was posthumously inducted to the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as a member of Metallica in 2009. He also appeared in a 2011 Rolling Stone readers' poll recognizing the greatest bassists of all time,[1] and in Rolling Stone's list of the 50 greatest bass players of all time.[2]

Death
Burton's final performance with Metallica on September 26, 1986 was hosted at Solnahallen in Stockholm, Sweden on the Damage Inc. tour in support of the Master of Puppets album.[23] Their next scheduled show at the Saga Theater in Copenhagen, Denmark[24] had their tour bus driving south overnight along European route E4 (now G 557). Band members complained that the bunks on their tour bus were unsatisfactory and uncomfortable. The story of how Burton won the bunk differs between the two band members; as Kirk Hammett stated on VH1's Behind the Music, he and Burton drew cards, and Burton picked the ace of spades, thereby getting the first choice of bunk. Burton told Hammett "I want your bunk". Hammett replied "Fine, take my bunk, I'll sleep up front, it's probably better anyway".[25] However, Ulrich's version of the event was that Hammett and Burton drew straws, while Burton drew the long straw, winning the choice of bunk.[26] Burton was sleeping when, according to the driver, shortly before 7 a.m. on September 27, the bus skidded off the road 12 miles [19 km] north of Ljungby, just north of Dörarp,[27] and flipped onto the grass in Kronoberg County.[28] With no safety restraints on the bunks, Burton was thrown violently through one of the windows of the bus, which fell on top of him right afterwards, killing him instantly. He was 24 years old.

The bus driver later claimed that the crash was caused by the bus hitting a patch of black ice on the road, but Hetfield later stated that he first believed the bus flipped because the driver was intoxicated. Hetfield also claimed that he walked a lengthy distance along the road unsuccessfully searching for the point in which the bus lost traction from the black ice. When local freelance photographer Lennart Wennberg (who attended the crash-scene the following morning) was asked in a later interview about the likelihood that black ice caused the accident, he said it was "out of the question" because the road was dry and the temperature around 36 °F (2 °C), too warm for ice. This was confirmed by police who, like Hetfield, also found no ice on the road. Ljungby detective Arne Pettersson was reported in a local newspaper to have said the tracks at the accident site were exactly like ones seen when drivers fall asleep at the wheel. However, the driver stated under oath that he had slept during the day and was fully rested; his testimony was confirmed by the driver of a second tour bus that was carrying the band's crew and equipment.[27] The driver was determined not at fault for the accident and no charges were brought against him.[29]

Burton's body was cremated and the ashes were scattered at the Maxwell Ranch.[30] At the ceremony, the song "Orion" was played. Metallica would go on to hire Jason Newsted from Flotsam and Jetsam to replace Burton on October 28, 1986.[31][32] Both Ray and Jan Burton appeared at Newsted's second audition, in which Jan Burton embraced him following his hiring, telling Newsted "You are the one, Please be safe". He would remain with the band until his departure on January 17, 2001.[32][33]

text:
There is a kind of legend that does not need a billion dollar reboot to prove it mattered. It only needs a living room, a kid who still believes a plastic dinosaur can charge across a carpet like a warhorse. Dino Riders is that legend. It is a fourteen episode cartoon from 1988, born to sell toys, aired in first run syndication inside the Marvel Action Universe block, and somehow it outgrew the cash register that made it. That is the first thing you are supposed to take away. Greatness is not always planned. Sometimes it arrives as a half hour of Saturday morning thunder, two ships ripped out of the future, and a prehistoric Earth that becomes the last battlefield two kinds of people will ever share.

The general sense of the story is this. A peaceful people called the Valorians lose their world to the Rulon Alliance, a coalition of cruel humanoid creatures led by the frog warlord Krulos. In a last desperate flight they fire the Space Time Energy Projector, the S.T.E.P., hoping to vanish from the hunt. The machine does not send them somewhere safe. It hurls them sixty five million years backward onto a planet still ruled by dinosaurs, and because a Rulon tractor beam is locked onto their ship at the worst possible second, the enemy comes with them. Stranded, both sides look at the same living mountains of bone and muscle and decide those creatures will decide the war. That is all the plot you need to know before the lesson starts working on you. The rest of the series is not a travelogue of fights. It is a repeated test of one question. When you meet a power larger than yourself, do you ask it to stand with you, or do you clamp a machine on its mind and force it to march?

That question is why Dino Riders stands apart from almost everything in its field. Other eighties cartoons sold transformation, secret identities, or a weekly monster of the week. Other dinosaur stories sold wonder, then later they sold terror. Dino Riders sold a moral contrast so clean a child can feel it before he can name it. The Valorians wear AMP necklaces, Amplified Mental Projectors, and they use them to speak across the gap between species. They listen. They wait. They ride what chooses them. Questar, their leader, does not treat a Diplodocus like a truck. He treats it like an ally whose life is not cheaper than his own. The Rulons answer the same wilderness with Brain Boxes, devices that steal will and turn a Tyrannosaurus into a walking gun platform. One side builds a camp and calls the animals friends. The other side builds an army and calls the animals inventory. Watch that difference long enough and you are not just watching good guys beat bad guys. You are watching the difference between partnership and domination, and that is a lesson that does not expire in 2026 or any other year.

You are supposed to take away that peace is not the same thing as weakness. The Valorians are not warriors by nature. Their culture had already chosen harmony, telepathy, study, and a life that did not require an empire. History still kicked the door in. The cartoon does not apologize for that. It says a gentle people may still have to fight when a tyrant follows them across time itself. Questar is strong willed and easy to follow because he can give an order without becoming the thing he is fighting. Mind Zei, blind and still the wisest man in the camp, proves that sight is not the only way to know a battlefield. Serena can heal, and the show is honest enough to admit healing costs her. Yungstar is young, proud, hungry for the charge, and the story lets pride walk him into trouble so you can see dedication survive the bruise. These are not identity sermons. They are old morals wearing laser saddles. Courage. Loyalty. Self control. Respect for living things. The duty of a leader to ask for help. The duty of a follower not to mistake impulse for bravery. You can hand this to a child in 2026 and you will not have to sit beside the screen translating a new ideology into the mouths of dinosaurs. The good people look like people. The villains look like predators who learned to walk upright and never learned to stop taking. That clarity is not simple minded. It is the reason the show still feels like a campfire instead of a pamphlet.

What makes it unique is the collision nobody else quite dared to stage at this volume. Space opera falls into the Cretaceous. A crystal that punches holes in time becomes the prize both armies want, because whoever holds the S.T.E.P. can leave prehistory and finish the war in the future. Until that happens, the most advanced weapons in the universe are strapped to animals that never asked to be in anyone’s war. The image should be ridiculous. A Quetzalcoatlus with wing guns. A Triceratops wearing armor like a moving fortress. A T Rex carrying Krulos in a command tower while the jaws work and the lasers turn. It is ridiculous, and it is also perfect, because childhood has always known that the sublime and the absurd live in the same roar. Before Jurassic Park taught a generation to fear the paddock, Dino Riders taught a generation to cheer the charge. It arrived after the original Star Wars trilogy had already made space myth common and years before dinosaurs became photorealistic gods of the multiplex. It stands in that gap like a secret handshake. If you were there, you remember the boxes more than the ratings. If you were not, you can still feel why a kid would stare at a shelf and believe the future and the deep past had finally agreed to share a toy aisle.

It is a masterpiece of a very particular kind, the kind that does not need three seasons and a lore bible to become a cultural icon. Fourteen episodes is a short life. That shortness is part of the legend. The show never got fat. It never explained itself into boredom. It never resolved the war so completely that the dream had nowhere left to run. The Valorians try to rebuild a society in a world that is not theirs. The Rulons try to steal the crystal, enslave the land, and climb back into tomorrow as conquerors. Episode after episode the same truth returns. You can armor a dinosaur. You cannot honor one by treating it as a tool. When the heroes fight, they aim at the riders and the weapons, not at the beasts trapped under the Brain Boxes. That single habit is one of the deepest things the cartoon ever taught. Even in a laser war, mercy has a target. The animal is not the enemy. The will that stole the animal is the enemy. A child who absorbs that will grow up with a cleaner instinct about power than a dozen speeches could give him.

Call it a must watch because it still does the rarest thing entertainment can do. It is fun first. The morals ride in the saddle instead of standing in front of the camera and clearing their throat. You get the thunder of herds, the glow of AMP light, the ugly genius of Krulos, the loyalty of a camp that has already lost a planet and refuses to lose its decency. You get a Saturday morning universe where good and evil do not need a committee. You get nostalgia that does not sour when you share it. So many old cartoons are loved and then quietly retired because the next generation is told the past is unsafe unless it is rewritten. Dino Riders does not require that apology. It is adventure, friendship, courage, and the warning that technology without character becomes a Brain Box. Pass it down and you are not smuggling a manifesto. You are handing over a story in which people who want to live in peace still stand up, still protect the weak, still refuse to become slavemasters just because the wilderness offered them a bigger set of teeth.

It became an icon because the toys and the cartoon fed each other until the idea was bigger than either one. Tyco did not stumble into this. After Christmas in 1985 a vice president named Jim Alley chased a thought that sounded like a dare. Put a rider on a dinosaur. Make the dinosaur look like a museum piece instead of a cartoon puddle. Give it armor, guns, a saddle, and if you can, make the giant ones walk. William Stout, the same kind of artist who understood that prehistoric life should look designed by God and weather rather than by a cute factory, helped set the look. The Smithsonian later took the animals, stripped the lasers off them, and sold them as serious models. That fact still sounds like a joke until you realize what it means. A toy line made to start a war in a child’s bedroom was accurate enough that a great museum said the bodies were worth keeping. First year American sales hit about thirty five million dollars. International sales went higher. There were motorized walkers, the Diplodocus, the Torosaurus, the Triceratops, and the T Rex everybody wanted because the villain always gets the most terrifying horse. There were mini comics in the boxes. There were two packs, traps, flying reptiles, and later an Ice Age wave with mammoths and saber tooth cats when the well of dinosaurs had been drawn down. The cartoon itself only ran from October to December of 1988, with early episodes living on VHS even before some kids saw them on television. Marvel published comics. Haim Saban and Shuki Levy gave it that pulsing eighties heartbeat. The voices came from the same golden bench that made other action cartoons immortal. Dan Gilvezan as Questar. Frank Welker as Krulos. Peter Cullen as Mind Zei. Rob Paulsen, Cam Clarke, Charlie Adler, Noelle North as Serena. The machine was commercial. The aftertaste was myth.

That is why it still stands out among others. Transformers made machines into men. Masters of the Universe made barbarians into space royalty. G.I. Joe made the evening news into a playset. Dino Riders made time itself the arena and then asked whether friendship could command a force of nature better than fear could. Jurassic Park would later prove that dinosaurs could be cinema. Dino Riders had already proved they could be cavalry. It is not better than those giants at every craft. It does not need to be. A classic is not the longest or the sleekest. A classic is the thing you can still explain in one breath and feel in your chest. Peaceful people hunted across time. Wicked people who would rather own a living creature than know it. A crystal that might send you home and might just as easily strand you forever. A leader who can command without becoming cruel. A child on the floor who understands, without a worksheet, that you do not put a cage on a mind if you can earn a friend instead.

Watch it for the lesson hidden inside the spectacle. Home can be destroyed and still be rebuilt if the people who survive refuse to copy the conqueror. Pride needs a bridle. Healing is holy and it is not free. The old and the young both belong in the same fight. A weapon is only as decent as the hand on it. The future is not guaranteed to the strongest army. It is contested by the side that remembers what living things are for. The Rulons believe dinosaurs exist to be broken. The Valorians believe the same dinosaurs can choose a side. Everything unique about the show, the armor, the telepathy, the time wreck, the toy shelf that looked like a museum exploded into a war, serves that single argument. That is why it is a masterpiece in the folk sense, the sense that matters more than awards. A short series became a password among people who grew up in the last years before dinosaurs belonged to one studio’s brand. It is a cultural icon because it fused three hungers that never get old. We want to go back to the age of giants. We want to ride what we fear. We want the good people to win without turning into the bad people.

The behind the scenes only confirms how strange a miracle this was. The cartoon existed because the toys needed a world. Marvel Productions built that world with South Korean studios, Hanho on the earliest episodes, AKOM on most of the rest, colors shifting, designs flattening, Krulos’s armor sliding from dark menace toward a brighter pink as the production changed hands. Whole episodes existed to showcase a particular dinosaur the company wanted on a shelf. Three episodes went to tape for the American market. An Ice Age adventure arrived later on video and pointed toward a new era the line barely lived to see. By 1990 the last wave was already feeling the cold. Mattel would buy Tyco. Talk of movies would come decades later. A revival of toys would flicker. Rights would scatter between toy closets and the old Marvel library that later sat under a much larger company. None of that machinery is why you should watch. The machinery is only the proof that commerce sometimes knocks a cathedral into existence by accident. They wanted a walking T Rex in a box that cost a fortune in 1988 dollars. What they also made was a story a father can still play without needing to explain away the souls of the characters.

So watch it. Not as homework. Not as a relic you defend with irony. Watch it as the thing it still is. A legend short enough to finish. A war clear enough to feel. A cartoon that thinks a child can handle wonder, danger, loyalty, and a moral as old as any campfire. Two ships fall out of time. One people ask the ancient world for friendship. The other people put a box on its brain. Everything after that is noise and glory around the lesson you are meant to carry out of the room. Do not become the rider who only knows how to command by stealing a will. Become the rider who is worth following because even a giant can tell the difference. That is Dino Riders. That is why it remains a must watch, a classic, and a piece of childhood that does not need to be updated to stay honest. It was never trying to raise a committee. It was trying to raise a kid who would look at power and still choose to be decent.
